newsitem.title: USA: Texaco says grounded tanker shuts gas line.
newsitem.headline: Texaco says grounded tanker shuts gas line.

text.p: Texaco Inc's Bridgeline Gas said a grounded oil tanker in the Mississippi River forced the closure of an 18-inch natural gas pipeline near Plaquemine, Louisiana, the company told Reuters Friday.

"As a precaution, we are in the process of bleeding the lines. Once that's done, they're going to try to shift the cargo to the bow and lift the stern," a company spokesman said, adding there are two 18-inch lines in the area but only one was flowing about 180 million cubic feet per day of natural gas.
The spokesman said the company has storage capacity in Sorrento, La., that can meet customer needs.

He said he was not sure how long it would take to dislodge the tanker, but once it was removed, the lines would have to be inspected. It was not clear whether the tanker was sitting on the lines, he added.
"We can get the lines running immediately, but I suspect we'll want to inspect them first," he said.
